title: Grant proposal summary for a high school ham radio club
summary: An earnest one-page grant summary: club purpose, student outcomes, budget ask, and how success will be measured.

blocks.title: Northridge HS Amateur Radio Club — equipment & licensing grant
blocks.body: We teach students to earn Technician licenses, make real on-air contacts, and staff public-service communications for school events. This summary asks for starter station gear and exam fees so interest becomes skill.

blocks.heading: Need
blocks.body: The club currently borrows a single VHF handheld and meets in a classroom without a permanent antenna. Students pass practice exams but stall before on-air confidence. A modest station — dual-band radio, power supply, antenna, and licensing support — turns homework into contacts and public service.

items.label: At least 12 new Technician licenses in the grant year
items.detail: Exam fees covered for students with need.

items.label: Weekly on-air practice net during the school year
items.detail: Logged; mentors from a local club invited.

items.label: Two public-service deployments
items.detail: e.g. fun run / field day-style demo for families.

items.label: Open station hours with adult control operator present

blocks.heading: Budget summary (example)
blocks.caption: No personal luxuries. Gear stays with the school inventory list.

blocks.title: Access
blocks.body: Exam vouchers and loaner handhelds prioritize students who cannot buy gear. Gender and grade diversity goals are tracked so the club does not become a closed friend group with radios.

items.title: Procure & install
items.detail: Antenna coordination with facilities; inventory tags.

items.title: License sprint
items.detail: Study sessions; first exam session on campus if possible.

items.title: On-air culture
items.detail: Weekly net; mentor nights; one public event.

items.title: Report & sustain
items.detail: Outcomes report to funder; next-year dues/booster plan.

blocks.heading: Closing
blocks.body: Fund a station that outlasts one school year of enthusiasm. Students will leave with licenses, logs, and the habit of communicating when it matters.
